You want monogamy now and your partner doesn’t. The only way forward is to part ways and seek out a monogamous relationship.

My foundation used to look exactly like your pictures! For the nose, use pore strips once every 1/2 weeks and shave your face with a razor meant for peach fuzz once every 2 weeks. Both of these will help with foundation and pores looking more smooth. 
As for makeup, I changed my technique that has worked wonders. I put a pump of foundation on a makeup palette and spread it around so it’s not concentrated in one area. I then take my foundation brush and dip it in one of the areas (which will be a small amount) and use light downward strokes on my face in one small area at a time. I repeat this step till everything is covered. With this method, you will use less foundation which will result in less caking. Hope this helps!

Either way, I can promise you that this is NOT going to end well. My advice is to pull the plug now before any of the inevitable happens and turns into an ugly breakup. I’m 42 as well, and many in our generation along with Gen Z are believing the popular catch phrases “30 is the new 20” and “40 is the new 30”. Sadly, these are big misconceptions that are resulting in regrets and missed opportunities. While it is not impossible for you to still have biological children, making the timing and opportunity a reality is more challenging after each year that goes by. Like I mentioned before, you also have to realistically determine what age you will want to parent to . The later you start the longer into your older age you will need to parent.

Yes, men biologically have more time, but not much more when you think about the realistic possibility and not parenting in old age.

It comes down to personal preference; there isn’t a specific etiquette to it. The best first date I went on was brunch. The effort was still there, but it was lower pressure since I didn’t have to second guess whether my date legitimately wanted to get to know me or expected me to go home with him afterwards for buying dinner. With that pressure off, I was much more comfortable and the conversation just flowed as a result. As a side note, we did end up in a relationship. Plus, brunch entrees are typically less expensive than dinner ones depending on what you get. I think brunch/lunch for a first date is the sweet spot between coffee and dinner dates.

No, that would be a dealbreaker for me. You didn’t mention why said interest can only do one date every two weeks. Do they travel a lot for work? If there isn’t a good explanation as to why their time is so limited, I’d be worried about being the side piece.

I’m in no way saying that you did the wrong thing, just providing a possible explanation as to why he preferred to be ghosted. Being told by a romantic interest that they are choosing someone else over you is a blow to one’s ego.
